blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At senior level, the cash flow statement is the truth test of everything else. An income statement can be shaped by accounting choices, but cash flow shows what actually happened. Did the company collect what it billed? Did it pay what it owed? Did it invest wisely, or burn through its reserves?

At Czarnikow, the executive team reviews cash flow weekly during peak trading seasons. They read operating cash flow to gauge the health of the core business, investing cash flow to track how capital is being allocated, and financing cash flow to manage decisions on debt and equity.

The best finance leaders read a cash flow statement the way a doctor reads vital signs. The numbers do not lie, and they tell you where to look long before a problem becomes a crisis.

items.q: According to the text, why is the cash flow statement described as "the truth test"?
options: It is the longest of the financial statements
It is reviewed only by senior executives
It replaces the income statement entirely
It shows what actually happened, unlike an income statement shaped by accounting choices
items.why: "An income statement can be shaped by accounting choices, but cash flow shows what actually happened."

items.q: What does the executive team read financing cash flow to manage?
options: The health of the core business
items.why: "...financing cash flow to manage decisions on debt and equity."

items.q: The doctor-and-vital-signs comparison suggests that a cash flow statement…
options: gives early warning of trouble before it becomes critical
is only useful once a crisis has already begun
is reviewed once a year like a check-up
items.why: Inferência: "they tell you where to look long before a problem becomes a crisis" — sinais vitais antecipam o problema.

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: A strong income statement alone proves a business is healthy
Reported profit can be flattered by accounting choices
Cash and profit should be compared over time
Operating cash flow reflects the core business
items.why: Inferência: o texto sustenta que o lucro pode ser moldado; só o caixa é o teste de verdade, então o organograma do lucro sozinho não prova saúde.

items.q: The phrase "burn through its reserves" implies that the author sees this outcome as…
items.why: Inferência: a expressão é posta ao lado de "invest wisely" como o contraste negativo — algo que o caixa revela e que se deve pegar cedo.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie apresentar a análise de caixa à mesa de finanças. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, before anyone celebrates the headline earnings, let me show you what the cash actually did. I have run a rolling three-year window — cash flow against reported profit, quarter by quarter — and for us the two lines track each other almost perfectly. That is exactly what you want to see. The profit we booked, we collected.

Now look at this second chart. Same period, one of our competitors. Their reported earnings climb beautifully, but their operating cash flow flattens and then diverges. Year after year, profit goes up and cash does not follow. Rarely have I seen a gap that persistent that turned out to be innocent.

I am not saying anyone is cooking the books. But when profit and cash diverge for three straight years, the revenue recognition deserves a question, and usually the answer is buried in a footnote. Read it ruthlessly.

My recommendation is simple. Do not take a single competitor's earnings at face value. Pull their cash flow, lay it beside the profit, and let the divergence tell you where to look.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What did Sophie find when she compared her own company's cash flow with reported profit?
options: Cash flow rose while profit fell
The two lines track each other almost perfectly
There was not enough data to tell
items.why: "the two lines track each other almost perfectly... The profit we booked, we collected."

items.q: What pattern does the competitor's chart show?
options: Profit and cash flow are identical
Both profit and cash flow decline together
Cash flow rises faster than profit
Profit climbs while operating cash flow flattens and diverges
items.why: "their reported earnings climb beautifully, but their operating cash flow flattens and then diverges."

items.q: When Sophie says "I am not saying anyone is cooking the books," she is most likely…
options: changing the subject to her own company
dismissing the whole analysis as unimportant
signalling suspicion while remaining professionally careful
items.why: Inferência: ela nega a acusação direta mas mantém a desconfiança — cautela profissional, não inocência.

items.q: Why does Sophie tell the team to read the footnote "ruthlessly"?
options: Footnotes are shorter than the main statements
The footnote contains the share price
The explanation for the profit-cash gap is usually hidden there
items.why: "the revenue recognition deserves a question, and usually the answer is buried in a footnote."

items.q: Rarely have I seen a gap that persistent that turned out to be innocent — what is Sophie implying?
options: Persistent divergence is almost always a warning sign
She has never seen a gap like this before
items.why: Inferência: a inversão "Rarely have I seen..." reforça que, na experiência dela, uma divergência persistente quase nunca é inocente.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The cash flow statement is the truth test of everything else." A truth test is…
options: a check that reveals whether a claim is genuine
a legal audit required by regulators
items.why: Truth test = teste de verdade: o que confirma se o resto é real.

items.q: "They used aggressive accrual judgement to book revenue a quarter early." This refers to…
options: the timing decisions in matching income and expenses
the choice of currency for reporting
items.why: Accrual judgement = julgamento de competência: quando reconhecer receitas e despesas.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The margins looked ___, but the cash never arrived to back them up."
items.why: Flattering = favorável, lisonjeiro: parece bom na superfície.

items.q: "We track it over a rolling window rather than a single year." A rolling window is…
options: a continuously moving span of time
items.why: Rolling window = janela contínua: um período que avança no tempo, não um ponto fixo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "When cash and profit ___ for years, something in the numbers needs explaining."
items.why: To diverge = divergir: as duas linhas se afastam uma da outra.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de finanças e análise. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Their team learned to dress up the numbers before every earnings call." To dress up the numbers means to…
options: present them more favourably than reality warrants
format them in a new template
items.why: To dress up = enfeitar: fazer os números parecerem melhores do que são.

items.q: "Do not take those earnings at face value." This means do not…
options: accept them as true without checking
items.why: At face value = pelo valor aparente: aceitar sem questionar.

items.q: "The explanation was buried in a footnote." This means it was…
options: hidden in small print easy to overlook
explained by the auditor in person
items.why: Buried in a footnote = enterrado numa nota de rodapé: presente, mas escondido no miúdo.

items.q: "We need to drill down into the operating cash line." To drill down into something is to…
items.why: Drill down into = descer aos detalhes: examinar em profundidade.

items.q: "When the trend held for three years, the gap raised a red flag." This means it…
items.why: Raise a red flag = levantar um sinal de alerta: algo que pede investigação.
